question: Match these exclusive sign shapes from Table 2A-1 to their uses: octagon, circle, and pennant.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Per Table 2A-1, the octagon is used exclusively for the Stop (R1-1) sign, the circle exclusively for the Grade Crossing Advance Warning (W10-1) sign, and the pennant (isosceles triangle with longer axis horizontal, pointed right) exclusively for the No Passing Zone (W14-3) sign. Each of these shapes is limited to the sign indicated, and each of those signs must in turn use exclusively the shape shown. Standards (mandatory): - "Particular shapes, as shown in Table 2A-1, shall be used exclusively for specific signs or series of signs, unless otherwise provided in this Manual for a particular sign or class of signs." Table 2A-1 lists: "Octagon* Stop (R1-1)** … Circle* Grade Crossing Advance Warning (W10-1)** Pennant (Isosceles Triangle with longer axis horizontal, pointed right)* No Passing Zone (W14-3)**" - Per the table's footnotes: "* This shape shall be limited exclusively to the sign(s) indicated." and "** This sign shall be exclusively the shape shown." - "Note: Signs with standardized designs shall not be modified to accommodate a different shape except as provided in this Manual." Guidance (recommended): - "Shapes that are exclusive to a particular sign (such as an octagon for STOP, a pennant for NO PASSING ZONE, or a circle for Railroad Advance) should not be obscured by another sign mounted on the back of the same assembly protruding or extending beyond the edge of the sign with the exclusive shape." Methods to consider instead include separate mountings, increasing the size of the exclusive-shape sign, or increasing its mounting height. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2A-1 pairing Octagon with Stop (R1-1), Circle with Grade Crossing Advance Warning (W10-1), and Pennant with No Passing Zone (W14-3). [Image 2] shows the full Section 2A.05 Shapes page containing Table 2A-1 and its footnotes. [Image 4] shows the NO PASSING ZONE Sign (W14-3) standard confirming the sign "shall be a pennant-shaped isosceles triangle with its longer axis horizontal and pointing to the right." Citations: - Section 2A.05 Standard §1 (p.42) - Section 2A.05 Guidance §3 (p.42) - Table 2A-1 (p.42)
gold_answer: Octagon: STOP; circle: Grade Crossing Advance Warning; pennant: NO PASSING ZONE.
